newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan futures seen steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan futures seen steady to easier.

text.p: Japan's rubber futures markets are likely to be steady to easier this week amid the widespread view that bumper rubber stocks will not decline sharply after their recent falls, traders said on Monday.

They said Japanese traders had bought a large amount of Thai benchmark ribbed smoked sheet (RSS) recently, taking advantage of a narrowing price difference between local prices and prices in Thailand, and they feared the purchases could push up rubber stocks from next year.
The purchases were believed to total about 30,000 tonnes, probably for January or February shipment, although the figures have not been confirmed.
The benchmark May contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 141.9 yen per kilogram, down from 142.5 yen last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark May contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 142.7 yen, up from 142.5 yen last Friday.

"Japan's rubber stocks could fall in the near term, but may start rising again from next year. Except for the stock factor, the market lacks incentives and the energy to push up prices," one trader said.
Rubber stocks as of November 20 amounted to 41,516 tonnes, down 2,476 tonnes from November 10, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.
Good demand for winter tyres and the fact that Japan re-exported Thai rubber to China were the main reasons for the fall in the stocks, they said.
The traders said the market is likely to be spurred by technical factors because of a lack of fresh incentives.

"The market is focusing on whether the benchmark May contract will break under 140 yen per kilo. The market will be vulnerable to further downside risks if it breaks through that support level," one analyst at a commodity broker said.

The TOCOM benchmark May contract rose to 146.6 yen on November 26, backed by the high prices of the spot expiry the day before, but then fell due to caution that prices were too high and on hedge-selling by trade houses.
Another trader said the market could ease early this week but further falls could be limited on bargain-hunting buying.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at around $1.25 per kilo on a free-on-board basis on Monday, unchanged from Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users had eased and was quoted at 149 yen per kilogram against 152 yen on November 25.
